symptom: PC cannot reach server at 192.168.2.10
show_outputs: show ip interface brief: G0/1 192.168.2.1 administratively down/down; ping 192.168.2.10: 100% packet loss; Destination host unreachable
expected_fault: Router GigabitEthernet0/1 is administratively shut down

symptom: PC cannot reach server at 192.168.2.10
show_outputs: ipconfig: default gateway 192.168.1.254; ping 192.168.1.1: 0% loss; ping 192.168.2.10: 100% loss
expected_fault: PC has an incorrect default gateway; correct gateway is 192.168.1.1

symptom: PC cannot reach server at 192.168.2.10
show_outputs: ping 192.168.2.10: 100% loss; show vlan brief: Fa0/1 in VLAN 10 USERS; show interfaces fa0/1 switchport: Access Mode VLAN 10; Fa0/2 router-facing port remains in VLAN 1
expected_fault: PC-facing switch port Fa0/1 was assigned to VLAN 10 while the router-facing path remained in VLAN 1

symptom: DHCP client receives an address but cannot reach the remote server
show_outputs: ipconfig: IPv4 192.168.1.100, subnet mask 255.255.255.0, default gateway 192.168.1.254; ping 192.168.2.10: 100% packet loss
expected_fault: DHCP pool provides an incorrect default gateway; correct gateway is 192.168.1.1

symptom: PC cannot reach server at 192.168.2.10
show_outputs: ping 192.168.2.10: 100% packet loss; show interfaces fa0/2: FastEthernet0/2 is administratively down, line protocol is down (disabled)
expected_fault: Switch FastEthernet0/2 was administratively shut down

symptom: PC cannot reach gateway or server
expected_fault: PC0 is configured in the wrong IP subnet

symptom: PC cannot reach the remote server
show_outputs: ipconfig: IPv4 192.168.1.100, subnet mask 255.255.255.224, default gateway 192.168.1.1; ping 192.168.1.1: 4/4 replies; ping 192.168.2.10: 100% packet loss
expected_fault: PC0 has an incorrect subnet mask (255.255.255.224) causing incorrect subnet interpretation and preventing communication with the 192.168.2.0/24 remote network

symptom: PC cannot reach its default gateway
topology_note: PC0 (192.168.1.100) -> Switch0 Fa0/1 -> Switch0 Fa0/2 -> Router0 G0/0
show_outputs: show vlan brief: Fa0/1 is assigned to VLAN 20 while Fa0/2 remains in VLAN 1; show interfaces fa0/1 switchport: Access Mode VLAN 20; ping 192.168.1.1: 100% packet loss
expected_fault: PC-facing switch port Fa0/1 is assigned to VLAN 20 instead of the required VLAN 1, isolating the PC from its gateway

symptom: PC cannot reach its default gateway
topology_note: PC0 (192.168.1.100) -> Switch0 Fa0/1 -> Switch0 Fa0/2 -> Router0 G0/0
show_outputs: show interfaces fa0/2 switchport: Access Mode VLAN 10 (USERS); ping 192.168.1.1: 100% packet loss
expected_fault: Router-facing switch port Fa0/2 is assigned to VLAN 10 instead of VLAN 1, preventing the PC's traffic from reaching the router interface

symptom: PC cannot reach the remote server
show_outputs: ipconfig: IPv4 192.168.1.100, subnet mask 255.255.255.0, default gateway 192.168.1.254; ping 192.168.1.1: 4/4 replies; ping 192.168.2.10: 100% packet loss
expected_fault: PC0 has an incorrect default gateway (192.168.1.254 instead of 192.168.1.1), preventing traffic from reaching the remote network

symptom: DNS configuration is incorrect
show_outputs: ipconfig /all: IPv4 192.168.1.100, gateway 192.168.1.1, DHCP server 192.168.2.10, DNS server 192.168.1.254; direct ping to 192.168.2.10 succeeds 4/4
expected_fault: PC0 is configured with an incorrect DNS server address (192.168.1.254 instead of 192.168.2.10), which can cause hostname resolution failures

symptom: PC cannot obtain an IP address from DHCP
show_outputs: DHCP service on Server0 is disabled; PC0 requests DHCP but does not receive the expected 192.168.1.100 address and gateway 192.168.1.1
expected_fault: DHCP service is unavailable on Server0, so PC0 cannot obtain a valid network configuration automatically

symptom: PC receives incorrect default gateway from DHCP
show_outputs: ipconfig /all: IPv4 192.168.1.100, subnet mask 255.255.255.0, default gateway 192.168.1.254, DHCP server 192.168.2.10; DHCP successfully assigns the IP but provides the wrong gateway
expected_fault: DHCP pool is configured with an incorrect default gateway (192.168.1.254 instead of 192.168.1.1)

symptom: PC receives incorrect DNS server from DHCP
show_outputs: ipconfig /all: IPv4 192.168.1.100, subnet mask 255.255.255.0, default gateway 192.168.1.1, DHCP server 192.168.2.10, DNS server 192.168.1.254
expected_fault: DHCP pool is configured with an incorrect DNS server address (192.168.1.254 instead of the intended DNS server), causing incorrect DNS configuration to be assigned to clients

symptom: Server is unreachable due to incorrect IP address
show_outputs: Server0 ipconfig: IPv4 192.168.3.10, subnet mask 255.255.255.0, default gateway 192.168.2.1; ping 192.168.2.10: 100% packet loss
expected_fault: Server0 is configured with an IP address from the wrong subnet (192.168.3.0/24) instead of 192.168.2.0/24

symptom: Server cannot communicate with the remote network because the server has an incorrect default gateway
show_outputs: Server0 IP configuration shows an incorrect default gateway; local connectivity may work but communication through the router fails
expected_fault: Server0 has a wrong default gateway

symptom: PC cannot reach server due to incorrect server subnet mask
show_outputs: Server0 ipconfig: IPv4 192.168.2.10, subnet mask 255.255.255.224, default gateway 192.168.2.1; Server0 can ping 192.168.2.1 successfully (4/4); PC0 ping 192.168.2.10 fails with 100% packet loss
expected_fault: Server0 has an incorrect subnet mask (255.255.255.224 instead of 255.255.255.0), causing incorrect subnet interpretation and preventing communication with PC0

symptom: PC cannot reach server due to incorrect server default gateway
show_outputs: Server0 ipconfig: IPv4 192.168.2.10, subnet mask 255.255.255.0, default gateway 192.168.2.254; Server0 can ping 192.168.2.1 successfully (4/4); PC0 ping 192.168.2.10 fails with 100% packet loss
expected_fault: Server0 is configured with an incorrect default gateway (192.168.2.254 instead of 192.168.2.1), preventing return traffic from reaching the remote PC

symptom: PC cannot reach server because router interface G0/1 is shut down
show_outputs: show ip interface brief: GigabitEthernet0/1 is administratively down/down; ping 192.168.2.10 from PC0: 100% packet loss
expected_fault: Router GigabitEthernet0/1 is administratively shut down, disconnecting the 192.168.2.0/24 network from the router

symptom: PC cannot reach gateway or server because switch port Fa0/1 is shut down
show_outputs: PC0 ping 192.168.1.1: 100% packet loss; PC0 ping 192.168.2.10: 100% packet loss; Switch0 Fa0/1 was administratively shut down
expected_fault: PC-facing switch port Fa0/1 is administratively disabled, disconnecting PC0 from the network

symptom: PC cannot reach gateway or server because router G0/0 has an incorrect IP address
show_outputs: Router G0/0 is configured as 192.168.10.1 instead of 192.168.1.1; ping 192.168.1.1: 100% packet loss; ping 192.168.2.10: 100% packet loss
expected_fault: Router G0/0 has an incorrect IPv4 address, so the PC's 192.168.1.0/24 network no longer has its expected gateway

symptom: PC can reach its gateway but cannot reach the server because router G0/1 has an incorrect IP address
show_outputs: PC0 ping 192.168.1.1: 4/4 replies; PC0 ping 192.168.2.10: 0/4 replies with Destination host unreachable
expected_fault: Router G0/1 is configured with 192.168.20.1 instead of 192.168.2.1, disconnecting the server subnet from its expected router interface

symptom: PC cannot reach gateway or server because PC0 has an incorrect IP address
show_outputs: PC0 ipconfig: IPv4 192.168.3.100, subnet mask 255.255.255.0, default gateway 192.168.1.1; ping 192.168.1.1: 100% packet loss; ping 192.168.2.10: 100% packet loss
expected_fault: PC0 is configured with an IP address from the wrong subnet (192.168.3.0/24) instead of the 192.168.1.0/24 LAN

symptom: DNS resolution fails because the DNS service on Server0 is disabled
show_outputs: Ping 192.168.2.10 succeeds with 4/4 replies, but nslookup to DNS server 192.168.2.10 times out; Server0 DNS Service is OFF
expected_fault: Server0 DNS service is disabled, so clients can reach the server by IP but DNS queries cannot be processed

symptom: Web access to Server0 fails because the HTTP service is disabled
show_outputs: Web Browser access to http://192.168.2.10 returns Server Reset Connection; ping 192.168.2.10 succeeds with 4/4 replies and 0% loss
expected_fault: Server0 HTTP service is disabled while network connectivity to the server remains available

symptom: PC cannot obtain an IP address because the DHCP service is disabled
show_outputs: PC0 configured for DHCP receives IPv4 address 0.0.0.0, subnet mask 0.0.0.0, and default gateway 0.0.0.0
expected_fault: Server0 DHCP service is disabled, so PC0 cannot obtain a valid network configuration automatically

symptom: PC receives an incorrect default gateway from DHCP and cannot reach the remote server
show_outputs: PC0 receives gateway 192.168.1.254 instead of 192.168.1.1; ping 192.168.1.1 succeeds 4/4, while ping 192.168.2.10 fails 4/4
expected_fault: DHCP pool distributes an invalid default gateway, preventing PC0 from routing traffic to the 192.168.2.0/24 network

symptom: DNS resolution fails because DHCP provides an incorrect DNS server
show_outputs: PC0 receives DNS server 192.168.1.254; ping 192.168.2.10 succeeds 4/4, but nslookup server.local times out against 192.168.1.254
expected_fault: DHCP pool distributes an incorrect DNS server address, preventing clients from resolving DNS names

symptom: FTP connection fails because the FTP service on Server0 is disabled
show_outputs: FTP connection to 192.168.2.10 returns Ftp peer reset; ping to 192.168.2.10 succeeds with 4/4 replies and 0% loss
expected_fault: Server0 FTP service is disabled while IP connectivity to the server remains available

symptom: FTP authentication fails because the client uses invalid FTP account credentials
show_outputs: FTP connection reaches Server0 successfully, but login fails with 'No such Account' after username/password authentication
expected_fault: FTP service is available, but the supplied FTP account credentials are invalid

symptom: FTP file download fails because the user's Read permission is disabled
show_outputs: FTP login succeeds and directory listing works, but get sampleFile.txt fails with 550 permission denied
expected_fault: The FTP account can connect and list files but does not have Read permission for file downloads
